    **Spectrum of Ecstasy**
    
    This is not to say that there is no place for intellect - it is a valuable capacity. Intellect functions brilliantly in its own sphere; this is not in question. The problem with intellect is that we use it to distract ourselves from direct experience. In this web of contrivances we use our intellect abusively to judge perception as good, bad or indifferent, and we become conditioned to this.
    
    Although from the non-dual perspective, the mechanics of confusion are completely obvious, they are actually far from obvious when we are caught up in them, and occluded within these bizarre procedures. All freshness of experience is lost. It is a bit like living on week-old crusts and trying to enjoy them - unsatisfying. You can splash them with water, toast them; and maybe, with enough jam or honey, they might pass for food. But you know you would be better off eating fresh bread.
    
    We contrive our perception according to habitual judgements; and it is therefore indirect. We see everything according to categories, We create versions of the world with stylised perception; and our response to them, is to assume that they are real. As a result of this, our reactions, interactions and relationships can become severely distorted. There is no real experience, no real perception, and no real world.
    
    In order to allow space for experience to be precisely what it is, we need to stop grasping at the phenomena we perceive. We need to loosen our obsession with relating to phenomena as a series of possible reference points. We seem to have a driving compulsion to understand everything we perceive in terms of our working body of knowledge. We relate to everything in terms of categories. We see everything in terms of how it relates to something else that we feel we understand.

title: McGilchrist-pilled: the meta-thread that ate Twitter
summary:
Malcolm Ocean basically built a personal wiki-in-public around Iain McGilchrist’s “left hemisphere vs right hemisphere” attention model, and then used it as the skeleton key for *everything*: AI, Buddhism, design, meaning, dating, even why running out of toothpaste triggers nihilism. Trigger was May 2019: Ocean drops a “meta-thread of various threads” and keeps appending links like it’s a living document—constantly caveating “not the pop left-brain/right-brain BS, McGilchrist is different.”

Arc is: **trigger (meta-thread + early evangelism) → peak (2019–2020: “LH takeover” explains modernity + the big intro thread) → outcome (2021+: it’s just “the water you’re swimming in,” plus practical off-ramps).** The peak moments are Ocean’s 2019 “AI bots are basically left hemispheres” riff off Janelle Shane—bots “when confused, it tends not to admit it,” plus the bigger claim that Bayesian updating assumes a fixed ontology and that’s the whole problem. Then Jan 2020 he welds it to Buddhism: impermanence and tanha-as-“grasping” are framed as left-hemisphere moves; awakening is basically “LH stops running the show.” May 2020 he drops the real artifact: a 40-ish tweet intro based on *Ways of Attending*, where the spiciest bit is McGilchrist-as-cultural-diagnostician: the LH is “Berlusconi of the brain,” hogging language/logic/linearity, and society starts looking like an LH-only reality (paper credentials over lived skill, explicit rules strangling democracy, cynicism, paranoia, mechanistic metaphors, etc.).

Then it cools into integration. Qiaochu Yuan names the phase change: “overlearning” is when you see a new hammer everywhere, and Ocean replies: yep, 2019 McGilchrist was that, now it’s internalized—“water you’re swimming in.” The community keeps extending it sideways: m_ashcroft’s Alexander Technique thread becomes the prized “practical bridge” (“If you stop doing the wrong thing the right thing does itself” → embodied, non-doing, wide spatial awareness), and Ocean’s like “this is gonna be big” because McGilchrist didn’t give pragmatic training advice. Later the model stays generative in smaller sparks: Yash Kaf says dating is broken because people try to date in a “LEFT-BRAINED way”; slimepriestess pushes back with a “three hemispheres” / id–creative_self–analytic_self remix; Ocean keeps pulling everything back into the same folder.

Why care: this is what it looks like when a niche framework turns into a shared dialect for a little corner of Twitter—people use “LH takeover,” “ways of attending,” “grasping,” “overlearning,” and “Alexander Technique as RH access” as shorthand for arguing about cognition, culture, and practice. Even if you think McGilchrist is overfit, the residue is real: it becomes a *portable* way to accuse someone (or yourself) of living inside the map instead of the territory, and then point to concrete practices for getting back out.
